claims.text: The gleaming white Sacré-Cœur Basilica sits at the very summit of Montmartre, overlooking the entire city of Paris.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Construction took place between 1875 and 1914, serving as a grand act of national penitence after the bloody 1870 Franco-Prussian War.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Because it was built over the site of the Paris Commune uprising, it remains a highly controversial monument among some left-wing locals.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The building was designed in a unique Romano-Byzantine style, which was highly unusual for the period and completely unlike other Parisian monuments.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The tall campanile bell tower at the north end holds the famous 'Savoyarde', which is the single largest bell in France.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Inside, the lighting is kept unusually dim on purpose, contrasting the bright white exterior to create a deeply mystical atmosphere.
claims.subject: self
